```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
```

# REINF Experiment

## Step 1: Formatting data for IPM analysis

Load in the data

```{r}
dat = fread("../../data/lab_data/REINF_experiment_data.csv")
```

Plot the experimental data

```{r}
# Drop preliminary days
pdat = as.data.table(dat)[days >= -17, ]
pdat[days == -17, "days"] = 0
pdat$treatment = plyr::revalue(pdat$ttt, c("A"="30 days prior", "B"="6 months prior", "N"="Naive"))

pdat_medians = pdat[, list(median_load=median(ZE)), by=list(treatment, days)]
ggplot(pdat, aes(x=days, y=log(ZE + 1), color=treatment)) + geom_line(aes(group=as.factor(frog)), alpha=0.3) + 
                geom_line(data=pdat_medians, aes(y=log(median_load + 1), x=days, color=treatment), linewidth=1) + 
                theme_bw() + ylab("ln(Bd load + 1)") + xlab("Days") + guides(color=guide_legend(title="Treatment"))

```

Format the data for the Stan analysis. Drop all preliminary time points before day == -17 as these were just
swabs checking on individuals.

```{r}
# Split up the data by treatment
trun_dat = dat[dat$days >= - 17, ]
plot_dat = trun_dat
plot_dat[plot_dat$days == -17, "days"] = 0
treatments = lapply(unique(trun_dat$ttt), function(x) trun_dat[trun_dat$ttt == x, ])

max_days = 10 # Maximum number of days
max_frogs= 20 # Maximum number of frogs

# Lists to hold results
days_arrays = list()
load_arrays = list()

for(j in 1:length(treatments)){
    
    tdat = treatments[[j]]
    days = array(-1, dim=c(max_frogs, max_days))
    loads = array(-1, dim=c(max_frogs, max_days))
    
    for(i in 1:length(unique(tdat$frog))){
        
        frog_id = unique(tdat$frog)[i]
        temp = tdat[tdat$frog == frog_id, c("days", "ZE")]
        temp$days[temp$days == -17] = 0 # Day -17 is really day 0 
        
        # Check if there are two zeros and drop one of the zeros
        if(sum(temp$days == 0) > 1)
            temp = temp[-1, ]
        
        # Exclude frog 10 with only 2 swabs post-infection
        if(length(temp$days) > 3){
            days[i, 1:length(temp$days)] = temp$days
            loads[i, 1:length(temp$days)] = temp$ZE
        } else{
          print(frog_id)
        }
    }
    
    days_arrays[[j]] = days
    load_arrays[[j]] = loads
}
        
```

**How many different types of transitions are in this data?**

The treatment groups are represented by the heading "ttt", where
N=naive, A=recently infected (30 days prior) and B = distantly infected
(6 months prior).

```{r}
trans_type = function(x, method){
  
  n = length(x)
  x1 = x[1:(n - 1)]
  x2 = x[2:n]
  
  if(method == "0tonot0")
    return(sum((x1 == 0) & (x2 > 0)))
  else if(method == "0to0")
    return(sum((x1 == 0) & (x2 == 0)))
  else if(method == "not0tonot0")
    return(sum((x1 > 0) & (x2 > 0)))
  else if(method == "not0to0")
    return(sum((x1 > 0) & (x2 == 0)))
  else
    return(paste(method, "not recognized"))
    
}

transitions = c("0tonot0", "0to0", "not0tonot0", "not0to0")

res = list()
treat_names = unique(trun_dat$ttt)

for(trans in transitions){
  
  res[[trans]] = array(NA, dim=3)
  names(res[[trans]]) = treat_names
  
  for(j in 1:length(load_arrays)){
    
    tload = load_arrays[[j]]
    res[[trans]][j] = sum(apply(tload, 1, trans_type, trans))
  }
}

res
```

```{r}

# Number of data points contributing to likelihood
counter = 0

for(t in 1:length(load_arrays)){ # Loop over treatments
  treatment = load_arrays[[t]]
  
  for(f in 1:nrow(treatment)){ # Loop over frogs
    
    for(time in 1:ncol(treatment)){ # Loop over time steps
      
      if(time != 10){ # Last time step
        if(treatment[f, time] != -1 & treatment[f, time + 1] != -1){
          counter = counter + 1
        }
      }
    }
  }
}


```


## Step 2: Fit the IPM model as described in the Appendix


```{r}
# Fitting the stan model
stan_data = list("T"=3, "H"= max_frogs, "time_steps"=max_days, samps=load_arrays, D=counter, days=days_arrays)
```


```{r}
ipm_mod = stan("stan_models/reinf_ipm_model.stan", data=stan_data, 
                        warmup=1000, iter=5000, chains=3, cores=3)
```

Check model convergence

```{r}
# Check Summary
summary_matrix = summary(ipm_mod)$summary
summary_matrix[1:18, ]
```

```{r}
traceplot(ipm_mod, pars=row.names(summary_matrix)[1:18])
```

###  The initial transmission function

```{r}
colors = c('#1b9e77','#d95f02','#7570b3')


quants = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)
mod_prms = rstan::extract(ipm_mod)
naive_prob = rethinking::inv_logit(mod_prms$bt_init0)
treatA_prob = rethinking::inv_logit(mod_prms$bt_init0 + mod_prms$bt_tA)
treatB_prob = rethinking::inv_logit(mod_prms$bt_init0 + mod_prms$bt_tB)
trans_dat = melt(rbind(naive_prob, treatA_prob, treatB_prob))
colnames(trans_dat) = c("Treatment", "index", "prob")

# 1-month effect
quantile(mod_prms$bt_tA, c(0.025, 0.975))

# 6-month effect
quantile(mod_prms$bt_tB, c(0.025, 0.975))


trans_dat$Treatment = plyr::revalue(trans_dat$Treatment, c(naive_prob = "REINF-N", treatA_prob = "REINF-1mo", treatB_prob="REINF-6mo"))
trans_dat$Treatment = factor(trans_dat$Treatment, levels=c("REINF-N", "REINF-1mo", "REINF-6mo"))

pinf_plot = ggplot(data=trans_dat, aes(x=Treatment, y=prob, fill=Treatment)) + geom_violin(alpha=0.8) + 
            xlab("") + ylab("Probability of infection\nupon re-exposure") + 
            theme_classic() + stat_summary(fun.y=median, geom="point", size=2, color="black") + ylim(0, 1) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors)
pinf_plot
ggsave("../../results/initial_infection_probability_reinf.pdf", width=5, height=3)
pinf_plot = pinf_plot + theme(legend.position = "none")
pinf_plot
as.data.table(trans_dat)[, list(median=quantile(prob, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))), by=c("Treatment")]
```

### The loss of infection function

```{r}
library(magrittr)
zvals = seq(-1, 12, length=100)
naive_loss = sapply(zvals, function(z) rethinking::inv_logit(mod_prms$bl0 + mod_prms$bl1*z)) %>% apply(2, quantile, quants) %>% t() %>% as.data.frame()
treatA_loss = sapply(zvals, function(z) rethinking::inv_logit(mod_prms$bl0 + (mod_prms$bl1)*z + mod_prms$bl_tA)) %>% apply(2, quantile, quants) %>% t() %>% as.data.frame()
treatB_loss = sapply(zvals, function(z) rethinking::inv_logit(mod_prms$bl0 + (mod_prms$bl1)*z + mod_prms$bl_tB)) %>% apply(2, quantile, quants) %>% t() %>% as.data.frame()

naive_loss$treatment = "REINF-N"
treatA_loss$treatment = "REINF-1mo"
treatB_loss$treatment = "REINF-6mo"

loss_dat = rbind(naive_loss, treatA_loss, treatB_loss)
loss_dat$treatment = factor(loss_dat$treatment, levels=c("REINF-N", "REINF-1mo", "REINF-6mo"))

loss_dat$lgzoo = log10(exp(rep(zvals, 3)))
colnames(loss_dat) = c("lower", "median", "upper", "Treatment", "lgzoo")

loss_dat_reinf$ttt = plyr::revalue(loss_dat_reinf$ttt, c('N'="REINF-N", "B"="REINF-6mo", "A"="REINF-1mo"))
loss_dat_reinf$ttt = factor(loss_dat_reinf$ttt, levels=c("REINF-N", "REINF-1mo", "REINF-6mo"))
loss_plot = loss_plot + geom_point(data=loss_dat_reinf[sizeZE > 0, ], aes(x=log10(sizeZE), y=as.integer(sizeZENext == 0), color=ttt), size=2, pch=21) +
            scale_color_manual(values =colors)
loss_plot
ggsave("../../results/loss_plot_reinf.pdf",width=5, height=3)
loss_plot = loss_plot + theme(legend.position = "none")
loss_plot
```

### Get the statistics from the REINF model

```{r}
# 1. Loss effects
rethinking::precis(ipm_mod, prob=0.95)
```

```{r}
# 2. Stationary load
params = rstan::extract(ipm_mod)
treatB_stationary = (params$bg0 + params$bg_tB2) / (1 - (params$bg1 + params$bg_tB)) 
naive_stationary = (params$bg0) / (1 - (params$bg1))
quantile(log10(exp(naive_stationary)), c(0.025, .5, .975))
quantile(log10(exp(treatB_stationary)), c(0.025, .5, .975))
diff_btwn = log10(exp(treatB_stationary)) - log10(exp(naive_stationary))
mean(diff_btwn)
quantile(diff_btwn, c(.025, 0.975))
```

## Step 3: Project the best fit model forward for each treatment

Now we want to project these best fit models forward in time to compare
their fit to the observed data.

```{r}

ipm_sim_base = function(num, time_steps, params, treatment){
  # Simulating an individual frog trajectory from the fitted model (based on model ipm_mod8D)
  # 
  # num : int, a simulation number
  # time_steps : number of discrete time steps to simulate the model
  # params: A vector of ipm parameters
  # treatment: Either "naive", "A", or "B"
  
  times = 0:time_steps
  init_load = 0
  loads = array(NA, dim=length(times))
  
  # Set treatment coeffs
  if(treatment == "naive"){
    treat_coefs = c(0, 0)
  } else if(treatment == "A"){
    treat_coefs = c(1, 0)
  } else{
    treat_coefs = c(0, 1)
  }
  
  loads[1] = init_load
  
  for(i in 2:(time_steps + 1)){
    
    current_load = loads[i - 1]
    
    # Transmission
    if(current_load == 0){
      
      if(i == 2)
        trans = rbinom(1, 1, rethinking::inv_logit(params['bt_init0'] + params['bt_tA']*treat_coefs[1] + params['bt_tB']*treat_coefs[2]))
      else
        trans = rbinom(1, 1, rethinking::inv_logit(params['bt0']))
      
      next_load = trans * exp(rnorm(1, mean=params['binit0'], sd=params['sigma_init']))
      
    } else if(current_load > 0){ # Loss of infection or growth
      
      loss = rbinom(1, 1, rethinking::inv_logit(params['bl0'] + params['bl1']*log(current_load) + params['bl_tA']*treat_coefs[1] + 
                                          params['bl_tB']*treat_coefs[2]))
      next_load = (1  - loss) * exp(rnorm(1, mean=params['bg0'] + log(current_load)*(params['bg1'] + 
                                          params['bg_tB']*treat_coefs[1] + params['bg_tB']*treat_coefs[2]) + params['bg_tB2']*treat_coefs[1] + params['bg_tB2']*treat_coefs[2]
                                          , sd=sqrt(params['sigma2_growth']*exp(2*params['delta']*log(current_load)))))
      
    }
    
    loads[i] = next_load
    
  }
  
  return(cbind(loads=loads, time=times, simid=rep(num, length(loads))))
  
}

```

# AGE Experiment

Analysis and plotting for the AGE experiment described in the main text

```{r}
# Load in the zoo data
zoodat = fread("../../data/lab_data/AGE_experiment_data.csv")
```

Visualize the data by groups.

```{r}
ggplot(zoodat, aes(x=day, y=log(ave_ZE + 1), color=as.factor(treatment), 
                   group=as.factor(frog))) + 
            geom_line() + facet_wrap(~wild_or_naive)

```

```{r}
zoodat_dt = as.data.table(zoodat)
```

### Cleaning data

There are a number of points that need to be removed from the analysis.
In particular some frogs were treated with itraconozole at different points in the
analysis, and all points after the treatment need to be excluded.

```{r}
# Find the all days after itracon. treatment on week 1 or week 3
rm_itz_ind = ((zoodat$W1_ITCZ == 1) & (zoodat$day > 7)) | ((zoodat$W3_ITCZ == 1) & (zoodat$day > 21))
rm_itz_ind

# Remove the points where these conditions are TRUE
zoodat_noitra = zoodat_dt[!rm_itz_ind, ]

# Fix one mis-labeled point
zoodat_noitra$day[zoodat_noitra$swab_id == "Tahoe098_W0"] = 0
zoodat_noitra[tub == 17 & frog == 98,  ]

ggplot(zoodat_noitra[tub == 17, ], aes(x=day, y=log(ave_ZE + 1), color=as.factor(frog))) + 
            geom_line()
```

```{r}
ggplot(zoodat_noitra, aes(x=day, y=log(ave_ZE + 1), color=as.factor(treatment), group=as.factor(frog))) + 
            geom_line() + facet_wrap(~wild_or_naive)

```

```{r}
# Add tub density as a covariate
zoodat_noitra = merge(zoodat_noitra, zoodat_noitra[, list(density=length(unique(frog))), by=list(tub)], by="tub")
```

Plot the cleaned data

```{r}
zoodat_noitra$wild_or_naive = factor(zoodat_noitra$wild_or_naive, c('wild', 'naive'))
med_zoo = zoodat_noitra[treatment==1, list(med_val=quantile(ave_ZE, 0.5)), by=list(day, wild_or_naive)]

ggplot(zoodat_noitra[treatment == 1, ]) + 
      geom_line(aes(x=day, y=log10(ave_ZE + 1), color=wild_or_naive, group=frog), alpha=0.3) + 
      geom_line(data=med_zoo, aes(x=day, y=log10(med_val + 1), color=wild_or_naive), size=2) +
      theme_bw() + ylab("log(ZE + 1)") + xlab("Days") + guides(color=guide_legend(title="Treatment"))
```

## Set-up the model to fit the IPM 

```{r}
# Split up the data by treatment
trun_dat = zoodat_noitra[treatment == 1]
plot_dat = trun_dat
treatments = lapply(c("naive", "wild"), function(x) trun_dat[trun_dat$wild_or_naive == x, ])

max_days = 6 # Maximum number of days
max_frogs = 35 # Maximum number of frogs

# Lists to hold results
days_arrays = list()
load_arrays = list()

for(j in 1:length(treatments)){
    
    tdat = treatments[[j]]
    days = array(-1, dim=c(max_frogs, max_days))
    loads = array(-1, dim=c(max_frogs, max_days))
    
    for(i in 1:length(unique(tdat$frog))){
        
        frog_id = unique(tdat$frog)[i]
        temp = tdat[tdat$frog == frog_id, .(day, ave_ZE)][order(day)]
        temp = temp[day != 8]
        
        days[i, 1:length(temp$day)] = temp$day
        loads[i, 1:length(temp$day)] = temp$ave_ZE

    }
    
    days_arrays[[j]] = days
    load_arrays[[j]] = loads
}
        
```

```{r}
days_arrays
```

```{r}
# Fitting the stan model
stan_data = list(T=2, H=max_frogs, 
                 time_steps=max_days, 
                 samps=load_arrays,  
                 days=days_arrays)
```

## Fit the model

Fit the Stan model as described in the Appendix

```{r}
age_mod1 = stan("stan_models/age_ipm_model.stan", data=stan_data, 
                        warmup=1000, iter=5000, chains=4, cores=4)
```

Check model convergence

```{r}
summary_matrix = summary(age_mod1)$summary
summary_matrix
traceplot(age_mod1, pars=row.names(summary_matrix)[1:7])
```

### Growth of infection

```{r}
mod_params = rstan::extract(age_mod1)
zvals = seq(4, 11, length=100)
naive_growth = sapply(zvals, function(z) mod_params$bg0 + z*(mod_params$bg1)) %>% 
               apply(2, quantile, quants) %>% 
                t() %>% 
                as.data.frame()
treatA_growth = sapply(zvals, function(z) mod_params$bg0 + z*(mod_params$bg1 + mod_params$bg_tA) + mod_params$bg_tA2
                     ) %>% 
                apply(2, quantile, quants) %>% 
                t() %>% 
                as.data.frame()

naive_growth$treatment = "AGE-N"
treatA_growth$treatment = "AGE-12mo"

growth_dat = rbind(naive_growth, treatA_growth)
growth_dat$treatment = factor(growth_dat$treatment, levels=c("AGE-N", "AGE-12mo"))
```

### Plot the model predictions

```{r}

ipm_sim_age = function(num, time_steps, params, treatment){
  # Simulating an individual frog trajectory from the fitted model (based on model ipm_mod8D)
  # 
  # num : int, a simulation number
  # time_steps : number of discrete time steps to simulate the model
  # params: A vector of ipm parameters
  # treatment: Either "naive" or "wild"
  
  times = 0:time_steps
  init_load = 0
  loads = array(NA, dim=length(times))
  
  # Set treatment coeffs
  if(treatment == "naive"){
    treat_coefs = 0
  } else {
    treat_coefs = 1
  } 
  
  loads[1] = init_load
  
  for(i in 2:(time_steps + 1)){
    
    current_load = loads[i - 1]
    
    # Transmission
    if(current_load == 0){
      
      if(i == 2)
        trans = 1
      else
        trans = 1
      
      next_load = trans * exp(rnorm(1, mean=params['binit0'], sd=params['sigma_init']))
      
    } else if(current_load > 0){ # Loss of infection or growth
      
      loss = 0
      next_load = (1  - loss) * exp(rnorm(1, mean=params['bg0'] + params['bg_tA2']*treat_coefs +
                                                  log(current_load)*(params['bg1'] + params['bg_tA']*treat_coefs),
                                             sd=params['sigma_growth']) )
      
    }
    
    loads[i] = next_load
    
  }
  
  return(cbind(loads=loads, time=times, simid=rep(num, length(loads))))
  
}

```
